review_scope_notes: 191 ts/tsx files -> narrowed per token-budget rule. Grep hit-lists driven: console.log/error, `as any`/`as unknown as`, and Next.js server/data-fetch pages. Verified NOT reportable: all `as unknown as`/`as any` casts are test-only (*.test.ts[x]); the flagged console.error sites (ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:60, RealtorManagement.tsx:572, and the two app/[locale]/error.tsx boundaries) are legitimate catch-block handlers with user-facing fallbacks. Expert traced the six server/data-fetch pages (listings, listings/[slug], realtor/[id], account/listings/[id]/edit, inquiries, sell) plus every @ppt/reality-api-client hook consumer under app/ and components/. Only the public listings search page lacks an error branch, and the QueryClient (lib/query-provider.tsx) sets no throwOnError so app/[locale]/error.tsx never rescues it -> silent empty-state on API failure. Two low-severity i18n gaps found on otherwise-localized authenticated/public pages. 3 findings = cap reached; no additional passes.

evidence: app/[locale]/listings/page.tsx:145 — The primary public search-results page calls `const { data, isLoading } = useListings(filters, currentPage)` and never destructures `error`/`isError`; the file contains zero occurrences of `error`, `isError`, or `catch`. The QueryClient in lib/query-provider.tsx sets no `throwOnError`, so TanStack Query's default (do NOT throw) keeps failures in query state and app/[locale]/error.tsx never fires. On any listings API failure the grid receives `data?.data ?? []` (line 338) and silently renders the empty state — indistinguishable from a genuine zero-result search — on the app's main SEO/user path. Every sibling data page (favorites, inquiries, saved-searches, FeaturedListings, agency profile) DOES render an explicit error branch, making this a clear omission rather than a design choice.

app/[locale]/saved-searches/page.tsx:38,55 — User-facing labels are hardcoded English literals ('For Sale', 'For Rent', 'All listings', and the '€… - €…' summary) inside `getFilterSummary()` rather than next-intl `t('…')`. reality-web ships sk/cs/de/en, so Slovak/Czech/German users on this authenticated page see untranslated English copy. The rest of the file is otherwise localized, so these strays look like an oversight.

app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx:36 and app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx:114 — Public profile pages render hardcoded Slovak strings ('Načítavam…', '✓ Overený maklér') irrespective of the active `[locale]` segment; these components deliberately bypass next-intl (documented in the agency page header comment). Non-Slovak visitors reached via localized URLs get Slovak text on public, SEO-indexed profile pages.
